fixes.explanation: Gathering the tribes is a big, beautiful idea, but it's not in this verse. Paul says Christ Jesus "…will judge the living and the dead…" and he mentions His appearing and His kingdom (2 Timothy 4:1). So the charge to Timothy comes with Jesus as Judge in view. Good guess, friend, but that one lives in a different passage.

Nobody's packing for the wilderness in this verse. Paul says they "…will gather around themselves teachers to suit their own desires." (2 Timothy 4:3). Gathering around teachers is the opposite of going off alone. The teachers are right there with them.

Idols are a big topic elsewhere in the Bible, but Paul doesn't use the word here. He says they "…turn their ears away from the truth and turn aside to myths." (2 Timothy 4:4). Idols are standing in the wrong line, friend, because the word on this list is myths. I'd be pointing at the oven mitts and calling them the cookies.

Right. Paul says the Lord will award the crown "…not only to me, but to all who crave His appearing." (2 Timothy 4:8). He includes others in the promise. I'd say that's a pretty generous thing to say.

Look at the verse again. Paul says the crown is something "…the Lord, the righteous Judge, will award to me on that day…" (2 Timothy 4:8). So the text really does say the Lord will award it to him. Paul even names who hands it out.
